questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I'm studying biology so Australia caught my interest due to its nature. Friends who have been there have told me nothing but positive things about melbourne the city and vibe - which is true!

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: If you have the change you should definitely go! It has been the best semester!

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: melb uni website was easily structured. Use the handbook to find all the needed information on courses upon and after arrival. Give Stop1 a call is you need help - they are very helpful.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer:
Although I didn't use it, I am aware that Melbourne University arranges for airport pickup on the day of arrival. 
Additionally, there was an orientation week with a schedule of events and chances to get to know all the other exchange students.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Through a friend from back home who was already renting the apartment, my university friend (who I traveled with) and I were able to locate a home, and we simply transferred the lease.  Use the "Fairy Floss Real Estate" Facebook page if you're not that fortunate. I know a lot of people who have found success there.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I is really nice to live close to the city and atmosphere - 100% recommend! It is a lot more pricey to live on-campus than off campus. But on the other hand you future friend live next door.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: There were different steps and things to apply for, but melbourne uni were good to keep me updated on the different deadlines.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Stop 1 is helpful and there were a information meeting at copenhagen campus before and upon arrival.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes i applied for. I also change 2 of my 4 courses in the two first weeks after i got there. I was easy to change.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Do you self a favour and look thoroughly at all the courses melbourne uni offers. I found myself finding course i would have liked to have after the last deadline which is two weeks into the semester.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of the course is very much the same as we are used to at copenhagen university.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The attendance in the classes is the largest difference. In addition, there are assessments that must be completed throughout the semester in order to sit for exams.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
- Plant Biodiversity
- Insect shaping society
-  Australia Flora and Fauna
- Dancing the dance 1

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: It was really nice to have a course which was not in your own field, so dancing dance was nice and only 3 hours a week were we did some different dancing styles and moved our bodies.  I thought the course on plant biodiversity was incredibly interesting and cool, and I would definitely recommend it. The instructors were really motivating, and the courses also included some field trips.

questions.answer: no

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Coffee was less expensive than expected, which i took advantage of. Fruit can be quite expensive. But overall much the same as in Copenhagen.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I used uni fitness which worked very well.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were really many different clubs and activity for the students which is all presented in the orientation week.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I were in the sport club and mountaineering club.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Tasmania was definitely worth the trip. Together with some people I met down here, I did it during our spring break.  Also Great Ocean road is a must if you deciding to go to Melbourne. I visited Kangaroo Island as well, but I've also heard that Phillip Island is a fantastic destination.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer:
I had no trouble at all; people in Melbourne are incredibly pleasant and
kind.The
vibe is very nørrebro so if you into that atmosphere - it is the perfect fit.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Just talk to them - everyone is super easy-going and nice.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: none in particular.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: their kindness and openness to everyone they come into contact with. Furthermore, the atmosphere and minimal effort involved in living and enjoying their lives.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
- enjoy it! is is truly the best experience!
- There are more important things than school and grades.
- just do it

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: read the handbook carefully and make sure you have considered all the offered courses.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Having time to do what i want and only have to worried about me. And 100 % all the friends i have made and experiences i have had.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The most challenging part was all the practical things you needed to apply of before arrival. It is really time consuming.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
